entries.name: OS Command Injection
entries.summary: An operating system command is built or executed using untrusted input without neutralizing shell metacharacters.
indicators: User input concatenated or interpolated into a string passed to system/popen/os.system/subprocess
subprocess with shell=True and arguments built from external data
Unvalidated file names or parameters used as an argument of an executable
safe_patterns: Argument list without a shell (subprocess.run([...], shell=False)) or execv with a fixed argv
Strict allowlist of permitted values before execution
entries.fix_hint: Avoid the shell: pass the arguments as a list (shell=False / execv), validate against an allowlist and never concatenate untrusted input into the command.

entries.name: SQL Injection
entries.summary: A SQL query is built from untrusted input without parameterization, allowing the structure of the query to be altered.
indicators: Concatenation, % formatting, str.format or f-strings with external data inside the SQL string
Parameters coming from request/argv/form reach execute() without parameter binding
snprintf/sprintf used to compose the query before mysql_query/sqlite3_exec
safe_patterns: Parameterized queries or prepared statements with placeholders (%s, ?, :name) and values passed separately
ORM with parameterized filters
entries.fix_hint: Use parameterized queries: cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s', (uid,)) instead of building the SQL string.

entries.name: Code Injection
entries.summary: Code generated dynamically from untrusted input is evaluated or executed by the interpreter.
indicators: eval/exec/compile applied to strings that contain external data
User input used to build expressions or scripts that are then executed
safe_patterns: ast.literal_eval for literals only
Dispatch through a table of predefined functions instead of eval
entries.fix_hint: Remove eval/exec on external data: use ast.literal_eval or a dispatch table with values validated against an allowlist.

entries.name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
entries.summary: Untrusted data is deserialized with a format that can instantiate arbitrary objects and execute code.
indicators: pickle/marshal/dill/jsonpickle applied to data received from the network or from untrusted files
yaml.load without SafeLoader on external input
safe_patterns: Pure data formats such as JSON with schema validation
yaml.safe_load
Signed data (HMAC) verified before deserialization
entries.fix_hint: Replace pickle/marshal with validated JSON or use yaml.safe_load; sign and verify payloads before deserializing them.

entries.name: Path Traversal
entries.summary: A file path built from untrusted input is not normalized and may escape the intended directory.
indicators: User input concatenated to a base directory and passed to open/fopen/send_file without normalization
'../' sequences left unneutralized or absolute paths accepted
extractall on untrusted archives without checking the member names
safe_patterns: Resolution with realpath/resolve and a check that the result stays under the base directory
send_from_directory or secure_filename on the received name
entries.fix_hint: Normalize the path (realpath/resolve) and verify that it stays inside the base directory; use secure_filename or send_from_directory.

entries.name: Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input (Classic Buffer Overflow)
entries.summary: Data is copied into a fixed-size buffer without checking that the input length fits in the destination buffer. Out-of-bounds reads and writes (CWE-125/787) caused by unvalidated indexes or lengths also fall under this entry.
indicators: strcpy/strcat/sprintf/gets on fixed-size buffers with a source of unchecked length
memcpy/memmove with a length derived from external input and no comparison against the destination capacity
Length computations that can underflow or overflow before the copy
Index or offset derived from external input used to access an array or buffer without bounds checking
safe_patterns: Explicit len <= sizeof(dst) check (or allocated capacity) before the copy
snprintf/strlcpy with the correct destination size and truncation handling
entries.fix_hint: Check the length against the destination capacity before copying, or use bounded variants (snprintf, strlcpy) and handle truncation.

entries.name: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
entries.summary: An arithmetic computation on externally controlled values can overflow and produce a wrong size used for allocations or indexes.
indicators: Multiplication or addition of input-derived sizes passed to malloc/calloc/realloc without an overflow check
Conversions between signed and unsigned types on lengths
safe_patterns: Upfront overflow check (e.g. size > SIZE_MAX / n) or calloc with a separate count
Checked arithmetic functions (__builtin_mul_overflow)
entries.fix_hint: Check for overflow before allocating (SIZE_MAX / n) or use __builtin_mul_overflow / calloc with separate element count and size.

entries.name: Use After Free
entries.summary: A pointer is used or freed again after the memory it points to has already been freed.
indicators: The pointer is not cleared after free and is reused on a later path
Multiple error paths free the same resource (double free)
References to an object kept in other structures after it is freed
safe_patterns: Pointer set to NULL right after free and checked before use
Memory ownership with a single release point (goto cleanup)
entries.fix_hint: Set the pointer to NULL after free, centralize the release in a single exit point and do not keep references to the freed object.

entries.name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
entries.summary: A weak cryptographic or hash algorithm (MD5, SHA-1, DES, RC4) is used to protect sensitive data or for security purposes.
indicators: MD5/SHA-1 used for password hashing, signatures or integrity checks against an adversary
DES/3DES/RC4 used to encrypt data
safe_patterns: SHA-256 or stronger for integrity; bcrypt/scrypt/argon2 for passwords
AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 for encryption
MD5/SHA-1 used only for checksums unrelated to security
entries.fix_hint: Replace the algorithm with SHA-256+ (integrity), argon2/bcrypt (passwords) or AES-GCM/ChaCha20-Poly1305 (encryption).

entries.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
entries.summary: The server makes a request to a user-controlled URL, allowing internal services to be reached.
indicators: URLs or hosts coming from external input passed to requests/urllib/httpx without an allowlist
No checks on schemes, private addresses and redirects
safe_patterns: Allowlist of permitted hosts/URLs
DNS resolution and blocking of internal addresses (loopback, link-local, RFC1918) before the request
entries.fix_hint: Validate the URL against an allowlist of hosts and schemes, block internal addresses and disable unnecessary redirects.

entries.name: Cross-site Scripting (XSS)
entries.summary: Untrusted input is inserted into an HTML page without escaping, allowing script execution in the victim's browser.
indicators: render_template_string/Markup/mark_safe applied to user data
HTML built by concatenation with request parameters
safe_patterns: Templates with autoescape enabled and variables passed as context
markupsafe.escape on the data before marking it safe
entries.fix_hint: Keep autoescape enabled, pass the data as template variables and do not mark user-controlled content as safe.

entries.name: NULL Pointer Dereference
entries.summary: A pointer that may be NULL is dereferenced without a check, causing a crash or undefined behavior.
indicators: Value returned by malloc/calloc/lookup/parser used without checking for NULL
Error paths that leave a pointer uninitialized and then dereference it
Optional struct fields used without a check
safe_patterns: Explicit if (!ptr) check with error handling before use
Invariants that guarantee the pointer is never NULL on all paths
entries.fix_hint: Check the pointer (if (!ptr) return -ENOMEM;) before dereferencing it and handle all error paths.

entries.name: Divide By Zero
entries.summary: An externally controlled divisor can be zero and the division or modulo does not check it.
indicators: Division or modulo by a value read from input, a file or the network without a check
Ratios computed on counters or sizes that can be zero
safe_patterns: Explicit divisor != 0 check before the operation
Value validation when the input is read
entries.fix_hint: Check that the divisor is not zero before dividing and reject invalid inputs.

entries.name: Improper Input Validation
entries.summary: Input is not validated (type, length, range, format) before it is used, opening the way to other defects.
indicators: Fields of a packet, file or argument used directly as a length, index or offset
Missing checks on ranges and on consistency between fields
safe_patterns: Explicit validation of ranges and lengths right after reading
Parsers that reject malformed input
entries.fix_hint: Validate the type, length and range of incoming fields before use and discard inputs that do not conform.

entries.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
entries.summary: Sensitive information (uninitialized memory, secrets, internal details) is exposed to parties who should not see it.
indicators: Structures copied to the user without zeroing padding or uninitialized fields
Error messages or logs that include internal data or secrets
safe_patterns: Zeroing the memory before copying it out (memset/kzalloc)
Generic error messages
entries.fix_hint: Initialize or zero the data before exposing it and limit error messages to the necessary information only.

entries.name: Race Condition (Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization)
entries.summary: A shared resource is used by multiple flows without adequate synchronization, with outcomes that depend on timing.
indicators: Separate check and use of the same state (check-then-act) without a lock
Access to variables shared by threads or interrupts without a mutex or atomic operations
safe_patterns: Lock held for the entire critical section
Correct atomic operations or lock-free structures
entries.fix_hint: Protect the critical section with a consistent lock or use atomic operations, eliminating the window between check and use.

entries.name: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime (Memory Leak)
entries.summary: Memory or another allocated resource is not released on all paths, causing exhaustion over time.
indicators: Error paths that exit without freeing what was allocated
Reassigning a pointer without freeing its previous value
safe_patterns: A single exit point with cleanup (goto cleanup)
Automatic resource management (RAII, smart pointers)
entries.fix_hint: Free every resource on all exit paths, centralizing the cleanup in a single place.

entries.name: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)
entries.summary: The application redirects the user to an input-controlled URL without verifying its destination.
indicators: URL or 'next' request parameter passed directly to redirect()/HttpResponseRedirect
Checks only on the prefix or on substrings of the URL, which can be bypassed
safe_patterns: Allowlist of destinations or internal relative paths
url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme / is_safe_url before the redirect
entries.fix_hint: Redirect only to internal paths or allowlisted hosts, validating with url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme before calling redirect.

entries.name: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (XXE)
entries.summary: An XML parser processes external entities defined by the input, allowing local files to be read or requests to be made to internal services.
indicators: etree/minidom/sax used on XML received from outside with the default parser
lxml parser with resolve_entities enabled or with network access allowed
safe_patterns: defusedxml instead of the standard library parsers
Parser configured without entity resolution and without network access
entries.fix_hint: Use defusedxml or a parser with resolve_entities=False and no_network=True.

entries.name: Insecure Temporary File
entries.summary: A temporary file is created with a predictable name and not atomically, opening the door to race conditions and symlink attacks.
indicators: tempfile.mktemp / os.tempnam: they only return a name, the file has to be opened afterwards
Names in /tmp built from the pid, a timestamp or other predictable values
safe_patterns: tempfile.mkstemp, NamedTemporaryFile or TemporaryDirectory
Creation with O_EXCL and restrictive permissions
entries.fix_hint: Use tempfile.mkstemp()/NamedTemporaryFile(), which create the file atomically with restrictive permissions.
